newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds roll over in calmer trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds roll over in calmer trade.

text.p: *Australian bonds had a calmer session after the aggressive price swings in the past week and saw trade largely concentrate on the bond futures roll over ahead of Monday's expiries.
*No U.S. data due for release later today.

Australian bonds had a calmer session after the aggressive price swings of the past week and saw trade largely concentrate on the bond futures roll over to March ahead of Monday's expiries of December positions.

The benchmark 10-year bond yield appears to have made a tentative base just below 7.50 percent, although no one was willing to suggest that the turmoil in local and global markets had subsided, traders said.
"It's been a wild week. Basically people are tired of watching what's been going on, and have generally kept their business to book squaring and the roll over," one trader said.
The market had looked as if it was set for another major assualt to the downside after a bout of offshore selling in after hours trading but this wasn't carried to the dayside.

Trading action in the U.S. is likely to steer the market next week with only the November merchandise imports data due for release on Thursday, although turnover could be lighter as investors close their books for year end.

However, Monday morning's trade could be exaggerated by the final stages of the futures roll over before midday, although this has been relatively tame so far compared to the move from outright trading.

The local market underperformed U.S and Canadian bonds despite the partial rebound from the lows seen in afterhours trading. However, spreads are still below the levels seen prior to this week's surprise rate cut. New Zealand bonds gave up some ground ahead of Tuesday's RBNZ policy statement.
